Hi Maria — great to meet you over email. Thanks for the diagram and questionnaire, those help a lot.

Below is a short operational and security preflight checklist we use to validate a Zentrax private deployment. If you can provide the items in bold ahead of kickoff it will make the first session productive: 

1) Account & networking
   - VPC ID(s), primary CIDR(s), and target subnet IDs (public/private) for Redwood components. (please: VPC ID, CIDR, example: vpc-0a1b2c3d, 10.10.0.0/16)
   - Nat/gw and internet egress points; are there TLS intercepting appliances?
   - If peering or Transit Gateway is required, share route table ownership and expected prefixes to allow to Redwood.

2) Identity & service accounts
   - Destination AWS account ID and an IAM role ARN we can assume for provisioning (cross-account role).
   - List of admin users and email aliases for operational access and PagerDuty.

3) KMS and keys (this is a frequent blocker)
   - KMS provider (AWS KMS, CloudHSM) and CMK ARN if available.
   - Key usage policy and if customer-managed CMK rotation is required.
   - If using HSM-backed keys, indicate whether CloudHSM cluster is present and network placement.

4) Network security & firewall rules
   - Required outbound endpoints for telemetry, billing, model fetch (we typically need to allow redwood-managed endpoints; we provide a short list).
   - Port allowlist for mutual TLS and health checks (we will provide exact ports).

5) Data handling & retention
   - Any retention restrictions, egress restrictions, or compliance redlines (HIPAA, PCI, etc).

6) Access for testing & smoke validation
   - A bastion host or jumpbox IP for our engineers to run env validation; if not possible we can arrange temporary VPN.

7) Scheduling
   - Proposed kickoff times: Tue Mar 29 09:00-10:30 PDT or Wed Mar 30 10:00-11:30 PDT (we'll book a 90-min slot).

I'll attach our redwood_private_onboarding_template.xlsx (one-pager checklist) after internal review — sharing now: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/c/Onboarding-Private-Deployments.

Ben and Karthik are looped for KMS/crypto and routing questions. If Zentrax prefers an initial security-only sync we can do that too.

Best,
Mina Haddad

> Nat/gw and internet egress points

> KMS provider and CMK ARN
We're using AWS KMS for customer-managed keys. CMK ARN: arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/abcd1234-ef56-7890-ab12-cdef34567890. Key policy allows account principals and a separate security admin role.

> Access for testing & bastion

> Compliance notes
We are SOC2 in-scope and have some contractual data residency notes; our security team will join the kickoff to confirm retention requirements.

We are ok with Tue Mar 29 09:00 PDT for the kickoff. I'll add Maria, Eng infra aliases, and our security lead to the calendar invite once you confirm.

Mina — quick internal note while Zentrax finalizes kickoff scheduling.

1) KMS integration: AWS KMS CMK ARN is fine, but we need confirmation on two items from Zentrax security:
   - Does the CMK allow cross-account decrypt/GenerateDataKey usage for the Redwood provisioning role (we'll provide the role ARN)?
   - Is automatic rotation enabled or do you require manual rotation windows? Redwood supports either; if automatic rotation is enabled, we'll align our rotation schedule with your ops calendar.

2) HSM requirement: Maria indicated AWS KMS only, not CloudHSM. If Zentrax later opts for HSM-backed keys for attestations we will need to plan network adjacency for CloudHSM instances and an additional ops window.

3) Egress & telemetry: the outbound EIP pool Maria listed is workable. We'll provide a minimized allowlist for telemetry domains and upload endpoints (these are short-lived endpoints we maintain and provide as a CIDR/ASN mapping).

Proposed action: Karthik and I will draft the cross-account role policy and a minimal KMS usage RFC and share before the kickoff so Zentrax can pre-approve.
